description: A comprehensive study of the architecture, instruction set, assembly language programming, and peripheral interfacing of 8085 and 8086 microprocessors in Electronics and Communication.

sections.title: 8085 Microprocessor Architecture
sections.description: Study of the internal components and pin configuration of the 8-bit 8085 microprocessor.

key_concepts.explanation: An 8-bit register that is part of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). The results of all arithmetic and logical operations are stored in the accumulator by default.
The 8085 has 5 active flags that indicate the status of data after an ALU operation: Sign (S), Zero (Z), Auxiliary Carry (AC), Parity (P), and Carry (CY).
To save pin count, the lower 8-bit address bus and the 8-bit data bus are multiplexed together. The Address Latch Enable (ALE) signal is used to demultiplex them during execution.

sections.title: 8086 Architecture and Memory Segmentation
sections.description: Advanced architecture of the 16-bit 8086 microprocessor, featuring pipelining and memory management techniques.

equations: Multiplying by 10H in hexadecimal is equivalent to adding a zero at the end (shifting 4 bits to the left in binary) to convert the 16-bit segment base to a 20-bit address.

key_concepts.explanation: The 8086 architecture is divided into two independent units: the Bus Interface Unit (BIU) and the Execution Unit (EU). The BIU fetches instructions from memory and places them in a 6-byte instruction queue, while the EU executes them concurrently, significantly increasing processing speed.

sections.title: Instruction Set and Addressing Modes
sections.description: Various methods by which the microprocessor accesses and specifies operands or data for execution.

results: The data or operand is provided directly within the instruction itself.
Example: MVI A, 05H (Load the 8-bit data 05H immediately into the accumulator).
The precise 16-bit memory address of the data is provided directly in the instruction.
Example: LDA 2000H (Load the data from memory location 2000H into the accumulator).
The memory address of the data is stored in a register pair (usually the HL pair). The instruction refers only to the register pair.
Example: MOV A, M (Move data from the memory location pointed to by the HL pair into the accumulator).

sections.title: Interrupt System
sections.description: The mechanism to halt normal program execution temporarily to execute a specific Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) triggered by external or internal events.

results: Interrupts that can be disabled, ignored, or delayed by the microprocessor using specific software instructions (like DI - Disable Interrupt).
Examples in 8085: RST 7.5, RST 6.5, RST 5.5, and INTR.
Interrupts that cannot be ignored or disabled under any circumstances. They are strictly reserved for extreme system emergencies like power failure.
In the 8085, TRAP (RST 4.5) is the only non-maskable interrupt and possesses the absolute highest priority.

sections.title: Peripheral Interfacing
sections.description: Programmable peripheral chips utilized to connect the microprocessor to external I/O devices, sensors, and memory units.

key_concepts.explanation: A multipurpose I/O device containing three 8-bit I/O ports (Port A, Port B, Port C). It can be programmed dynamically in various modes (Mode 0, Mode 1, Mode 2) and features a specific Bit Set/Reset (BSR) mode for Port C.

A dedicated chip that allows direct, ultra-high-speed data transfer between I/O devices and memory without any microprocessor intervention. During this transfer, the microprocessor relinquishes control of its buses to the 8257 using HOLD and HLDA signals.
